Samples run on Android %1$s with light themes. Native labels use a minimum of 16 sp for readability, so default text sizes are adjusted. Selecting a version or theme does not change the OS.
Input clears when the screen is recreated. Results show only the character count.

The Material Scaffold arranging content with the library’s layout slots.
Inspect the horizontal separator supplied by each library.
Inspect the vertical separator in a 64 dp preview.
Inspect the deprecated Material 3 Divider function.
Read-only preview; this library provides no disabled appearance.
Material 3 renamed this API to HorizontalDivider. This sample still calls Divider from the pinned library.
Change the counter to inspect single-digit and wider number badges.
Inspect a status badge without text.
Choose any library icon and inspect its attached number badge.
Open a date picker dialog supplied by the selected theme or library.
Initial sample date: %1$s. Confirm applies the date; Cancel or Back keeps the previous date.
Open a time picker dialog supplied by the selected theme or library.
The sample starts at 10:30. Changing the clock format keeps the selected time. Confirm applies the time; Cancel or Back keeps the previous time.
Material 3 uses text input when this window is too short for the clock.
A card with library defaults and optional click handling.
A Material 3 card with its default elevation and optional click handling.
A Material 3 card with its default border and optional click handling.
A library surface with default shape, color and elevation, and optional click handling.
Tap the container to increase the counter.
Read-only container. Taps do not change the counter.
The non-clickable sample has no enabled state. Enabled applies only to the clickable sample.
Open an anchored popup with menu items supplied by the selected theme or library.
Selecting an option closes this sample menu. The disabled option cannot be selected.
Copies input values and starts a new target sample.
Inputs copied to %1$s. Started a new sample.
The source provider does not support this sample.
The target provider does not support this sample.
This sample has no inputs to copy.
This icon is unavailable in the target provider.
The target icon was kept because the source icon is unavailable.
Choose a date directly in the original inline picker.
Choose a date in the Android framework calendar supplied by the selected theme.
Choose start and end dates in the original Material 3 picker.
Date selections update the sample immediately. Use the original picker controls to change the date.
Enabled does not apply to this picker. This provider has no control that disables all date interactions.
The target requires a selected date.
Compare fixed multiline text from the original provider.
Inspect text and its checked state in the original framework widget.
Hello, Android.\nThis sample uses several lines.\nCompare text appearance and spacing.
Enabled does not apply to library Text. Its API has no enabled parameter.
Uses the theme\'s multiple-choice check mark when available. Use Checked to change the state. Tapping the text does not toggle it.
No multiple-choice check mark drawable is available in this theme. The checked value remains visible in feedback.
Choose a time directly with the original picker from the selected theme or library.
Enter a time directly with the original Material 3 time fields.
Changes apply immediately. Default setup is 10:30 in 24-hour format. The value is a time of day, not a timestamp.
These library controls have no Enabled parameter. They remain interactive when Enabled is off.
Enabled uses the original TimePicker API. Internal controls follow this device implementation.
Show the live device time with the original TextClock widget from the selected theme.
The original analog clock face. Deprecated since API 23; the framework still renders it with the theme\'s dial drawables.
The original digital clock. Deprecated since API 17; the framework still renders it as a ticking text display.
A counting timer driven by the framework Chronometer widget with framework buttons.
Shows the current device time and updates itself. The 24-hour switch pins both format fields so the display follows this sample, not the system setting.
Start, Stop and Reset drive the framework Chronometer. A running timer keeps counting and resumes after recreation; Stop freezes the elapsed time.
Deprecated since API %1$d. This framework widget is still available and runs on the current OS.
The original framework ScrollView hosting a fixed column of themed text lines inside a bounded height.
The original framework HorizontalScrollView hosting a wide row of themed text lines that overflows the panel.
Scrolling is free-form touch input on the real container. Scroll position is ephemeral and is not part of the copied setup.
The original framework ViewAnimator stepping through themed child pages with Previous and Next buttons.
The original framework ViewSwitcher animating between two themed child views.
The original framework ViewFlipper stepped manually through themed child pages. This sample does not enable timed auto-flipping.
The original framework TextSwitcher cycling localized lines through its internal text views.
The original framework ImageSwitcher alternating between two original framework drawables.
Previous and Next step the original container with its own transition. Copying carries the displayed child index.
The original framework FrameLayout stacking a centered label and a corner marker in one themed container.
The original framework LinearLayout distributing three themed children by equal weight.
The original framework TableLayout arranging cells through real TableRow children.
The original framework GridLayout placing four themed children in a two-column grid.
The original framework RelativeLayout anchoring themed children with alignment rules.
The original framework Space widget keeping an empty gap between two themed labels.
The original framework AbsoluteLayout positioning themed children at fixed coordinates.
A static preview of the real container and its themed children. The layout has no inputs to copy.
The original framework ListView backed by an ArrayAdapter, with a single-choice checked item that copies.
The original framework GridView backing three columns from an ArrayAdapter, with a single-choice checked item that copies.
The original framework ExpandableListView with real groups and children whose expanded state copies.
The original framework ZoomControls pairing zoom-in and zoom-out buttons that move a level counter.
The original framework ZoomButton image button that steps the zoom level on each tap.
The original framework ZoomButtonsController overlaying its controls on a themed owner view.
Zoom taps move the level counter; the level is the copyable input.
The original framework AdapterViewFlipper animating adapter pages through real framework transitions.
The original framework StackView stacking themed adapter cards with sliding transitions.
The original framework android.app.Dialog base class with a themed title and message, not an AlertDialog.
The deprecated framework ProgressDialog shown as a real indeterminate dialog.
AOSP toast artwork in a custom popup that disappears automatically.
The button opens the real transient window. Copying carries only the count of opens.
The deprecated framework TabHost with its real TabWidget strip switching themed tab content.
Tab taps switch the original TabHost content. Copying carries the selected tab index.
The deprecated framework Gallery scrolling adapter pages horizontally with a selected item.
The deprecated framework SlidingDrawer hiding content behind a real draggable handle.
The deprecated framework TwoLineListItem inflated from the platform two_line_list_item layout.
First line of the two-line item
Second line of the two-line item
The widget is deprecated but still renders. Copying carries only the visible selection.
The framework PopupWindow floating a themed content view anchored to the panel button.
The framework ListPopupWindow anchoring a real adapter-backed selectable list to the panel button.
The button opens the real popup window anchored to it. Copying carries the popup\'s reported state.
The framework Toolbar hosting a themed title, subtitle, navigation icon, and real action items.
The framework ActionMenuView presenting real menu items as horizontal action buttons.
Action and navigation clicks feed the last action state. Copying carries only that reported action.
The framework WebView rendering real HTML inside the themed panel.
The framework QuickContactBadge assigned to a fixed contact address.
A real framework WebView renders this themed HTML content.
The widget renders real HTML. Page scroll and navigation are never copied, and host Enabled does not reach page content.
Taps open the framework contact overlay for the assigned address. Copying has no state to carry.
The deprecated framework DialerFilter composing digits and letters into a filter.
Type into the real digits field. The composed filter text is the copied input.
The framework VideoView playing a bundled clip inside the themed panel.
The framework MediaController floating over an anchored VideoView.
Tap the anchored video to reveal the real MediaController. Its transport buttons drive the player directly.
The framework ShareActionProvider rendering the real share-target submenu in a menu item.
Tap the share action to open the real target submenu. Picking a target reports one share.
Material 2 BottomNavigation or Material 3 NavigationBar with real navigation items.
The Material 3 ShortNavigationBar for compact horizontal destinations.
The Material 3 WideNavigationRail that can expand and collapse.
The Material 3 ModalWideNavigationRail overlaying content as a modal rail.
The Material NavigationRail with real navigation items.
The Material TabRow hosting real Tab and LeadingIconTab items.
The Material ScrollableTabRow hosting real scrolling Tab items.
The Material 3 PrimaryTabRow with primary indicator and divider styling.
The Material 3 SecondaryTabRow with secondary indicator styling.
The Material 3 PrimaryScrollableTabRow for tabs that overflow the row width.
The Material 3 SecondaryScrollableTabRow for tabs that overflow the row width.
The Material Snackbar shown through a real SnackbarHost.
A snackbar hosted by the real SnackbarHost.
The Material ListItem row with real headline and supporting text.
The Material top app bar with a title and a real action item.
The Material 3 CenterAlignedTopAppBar with a centered title.
The Material 3 MediumTopAppBar with a two-row height.
The Material 3 LargeTopAppBar with a three-row height.
The Material bottom app bar with a real action item.
The Material 3 AppBarRow that overflows extra actions into an indicator menu.
The Material 3 AppBarColumn that stacks app bar actions vertically.
The Material modal drawer that slides over content with real drawer items.
The Material 3 DismissibleNavigationDrawer that can hide its sheet.
The Material 3 PermanentNavigationDrawer that always shows its sheet.
The Material 2 BottomDrawer that slides up over content.
A scaffold that hosts a persistent bottom sheet below its content.
A modal bottom sheet that blocks interaction with the content behind it.
The Material 2 BackdropScaffold with a concealed back layer revealed over the front layer.
The Material 3 PlainTooltip hosted in a TooltipBox that shows on long press or hover.
The Material 3 RichTooltip with a title and action inside a TooltipBox.
Long-press or hover to show the tooltip
A list row that reveals a background while swiping and dismisses past the threshold.
The Material 3 PullToRefreshBox refreshing its content on a downward pull.
The Material 3 HorizontalMultiBrowseCarousel showing many items at once.
The Material 3 HorizontalUncontainedCarousel keeping items at full size.
The Material 3 HorizontalCenteredHeroCarousel featuring one centered item.
The Material 3 SearchBar that expands full screen over its results.
The Material 3 DockedSearchBar that expands within its bounds.
The Material 3 TopSearchBar pinned at the top of its content.
The Material 3 ExpandedDockedSearchBar showing docked results for its paired collapsed bar.
The Material 3 Label that anchors a tooltip to its content while the content is pressed or hovered.
The Material 3 VerticalDragHandle that resizes its pane through a real horizontal drag.
The Material ExposedDropdownMenuBox anchoring a real menu to its text field.
The framework EdgeEffect glow drawn by a plain View while dragging its edge.
Drag across the view to pull the real EdgeEffect glow. The pull count is the copied state.

Cat visits and spacecraft progress can use optional notifications. Rich progress styles require API 36 for Android 16 and API 37 for Android 17. Delivery follows your current OS settings.

The bee artwork and its reaction are retained. This release has no separate mini-game.
Hold the robot until the flying Nyandroid screen opens.
Tap the bean to reveal its face, then hold it for the movable bean playground. A screen saver is also included.
Tap the K six times, then hold the Android logo to open the interactive dessert mosaic. A screen saver is included.
Tap the lollipop five times, then hold it to open the tap-to-fly obstacle game.
Tap the marshmallow five times, then hold it to open the multiplayer flying game. Developer-preview screens are included.
Activate the cat tile, choose food in quick settings, and collect visiting cats. Naming, deletion, saving, and sharing are retained.
Tap the O five times, then hold it to open the draggable octopus. Android 8.1 uses its separate logo entry.
Tap the animated P screen seven times to open its hidden drawing canvas.
Double-tap and hold the 1 to rotate it, then drag it into the 0 to form a Q. Tap the aligned Q seven times to open the nonogram puzzles. Icon glyphs come from the current OS.
Turn the dial to unlock cats. Enable device controls to feed, water, and play with cats, then manage the collection.
Set the clock hands to 12. Color bubbles, the palette page, a home widget, and retained cat controls are included. Dynamic colors use the current wallpaper.
Set the clock hands to 13, then hold the bubbles to cycle emoji. The palette, widget, cat controls, and beta screen are included. Emoji depend on the current system font.
Hold the logo to launch the full space simulation. Drag to steer, explore planets, and land.
Hold the logo for about six seconds to enter the space game. Space exploration, autopilot, and the space screen saver are included. System behavior follows the installed OS.

Hold the logo for about six seconds to enter the space game. Space exploration, autopilot, the screen saver, and optional live progress notifications are included. Rich notifications require Android 16 or later.

Connect all 17 dots in one stroke and return to the starting dot. Then hold the revealed logo for about six seconds to enter the space game. Autopilot and a screen saver are included. Rich progress notifications require API 37; space exploration works on older supported devices.
